newsitem.title: GERMANY: Former Kohl secretary goes on trial for spying.
newsitem.headline: Former Kohl secretary goes on trial for spying.

text.p: A former secretary in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's office went on trial on Thursday charged with spying for communist East Germany in the 1980s.
The woman, named by justice officials only as Karin H.-P., denied she had worked for East Germany's notorious Stasi secret police.
The 44-year-old defendant admitted she and her husband, who is also on trial, had friendly contact with Stasi workers but said she had not passed on any confidential documents.
Prosecutors said the woman, who worked in the chancellery from 1981 to 1989 first under Helmut Schmidt and then under Kohl, had spied for the Stasi under the codename "Britta".
Security officials have played down the severity of the case, saying the secretary did not have access to classified information.
